correctness.rationale: For p>=5,b>=2, the sum of lower p-adic layers is S_<b=(2^(a+1)-1)(p^b-1)/(p-1)<n/2; all permitted top-layer divisors below n/2 contribute <n/2, so no equality until the final proper divisor n/2, where equality would require integer 2^(a+1)-1 strictly between p-1 and p. For p>=5,b=1, at x<2^a total <4x<4*2^a<=n; thereafter until n/2 the 2-adic and p blocks cannot reach n; final sum n occurs iff p=2^(a+1)-1. For p=3,b>=2, exact layer formulas show strictly consecutive proper divisors straddle n: n/3,n/2 if a=1; n/4,n/3 if a=2,3 or (4,2); n/6,n/4 otherwise. For p=3,b=1, n=24 is unique nonperfect equality, all other a excluded by consecutive straddles; n=6 also even perfect. Direct independent exact divisor-prefix enumeration checked 1800 cases a<=12, b<=6, odd primes <103 and exactly four expected positive cases. Finite checks corroborate the unbounded proof, not extend its quantifiers.

final_claim: For all a,b>=1 and odd primes p, n=2^a p^b is an initial-divisor-sum number exactly when n=24 (a=3,b=1,p=3) or b=1 and p=2^(a+1)-1 is Mersenne prime (even perfect). Thus no such b>=2 and 24 is the only nonperfect Erdős–Nicolas example in this two-prime-support even family.
